tagline: From the Amalfi Coast to Capri to Sardinia — a coastline built for the water.
summary: Italy's most coveted destinations are reached by sea: the Bay of Naples and Capri, the Amalfi Coast, the Aeolian Islands, and the long crossing to Sardinia's Costa Smeralda. The summer traffic between Naples, Sorrento, Positano, Amalfi and Capri is one of the densest leisure-marine corridors in Europe, run today on packed hydrofoils and ferries. A clean, on-demand foiling tier is the premium layer between the public hydrofoil and the chartered yacht.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief tells the Italian coastal story, because it IS the water of the Bay of Naples and the run to Sardinia. The Naples–Capri–Amalfi triangle moves enormous summer volume on crowded hydrofoils on fixed schedules; the Amalfi-to-Costa Smeralda crossing is a long open-water haul reserved today for yachts. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns the bay crossings into smooth, dry, on-demand hops, and the Quanta-LR hybrid range opens the Tyrrhenian trunk to Sardinia that no day-boat can serve.

demand_signals.label: Bay of Naples volume
demand_signals.note: Capri, Sorrento, Positano and Amalfi draw millions of summer visitors, nearly all of whom move between them by sea on hydrofoils and ferries.

demand_signals.label: Costa Smeralda & superyacht hub
demand_signals.note: Porto Cervo and the Costa Smeralda are a global ultra-luxury and superyacht destination; demand for fast, discreet, premium transfers is structural.

demand_signals.label: Hydrofoil schedule saturation
demand_signals.note: Summer Bay of Naples hydrofoil routes run at capacity on fixed timetables — an on-demand premium tier relieves the bottleneck.

demand_signals.label: Long-crossing access gap
demand_signals.note: The Amalfi / Tyrrhenian crossing to Sardinia is a 230-nautical-mile haul today limited to private yachts — a long-range clean craft opens it as a scheduled service.

use_cases.body: Naples to Capri: the marquee Bay crossing, today a crowded hydrofoil on a fixed schedule — ideal for an on-demand, dry, premium foiling shuttle.
Capri to Amalfi: the iconic coast-to-island hop linking the bay's two flagship destinations, comfortably inside Pioneer II range.
Amalfi to Costa Smeralda: a long-range Quanta-LR Tyrrhenian trunk to Sardinia — a crossing reserved today for yachts, opened as a clean premium service.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Bay of Naples crossings — Naples–Capri (16 nm), Capri–Amalfi (17 nm) and the Sorrento–Positano–Amalfi hops — sit well inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Amalfi-to-Costa Smeralda Tyrrhenian crossing (~230 nm) is Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening a Sardinia trunk no battery day-boat can reach.

signature_routes.label: Naples ↔ Capri — the marquee Bay of Naples crossing
Capri ↔ Amalfi — the flagship coast-to-island hop
Amalfi ↔ Costa Smeralda (Sardinia) — the long-range Tyrrhenian trunk

transit_planning: For a tourism authority or a premium operator: an on-demand, low-emission water tier that relieves the saturated hydrofoil schedule across the Bay of Naples, and opens a clean long-range Sardinia trunk that exists today only by private yacht. Start with the proven Naples–Capri–Amalfi triangle on Pioneer II, then add the Costa Smeralda crossing on Quanta-LR.
competitive_landscape: Coastal travel today splits between public hydrofoils and ferries (affordable, high-capacity, but timetabled and crowded in summer) and private yacht charter (flexible but costly). Navier's foiling tier is the missing on-demand middle: faster and drier than a hydrofoil, far more attainable than a charter, and cleaner than both — with a long-range tier that opens crossings neither can serve on demand.
regulatory_note: Italian domestic maritime transport is regulated by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport and the Corpo delle Capitanerie di Porto (Coast Guard), within EU maritime-safety frameworks; passenger operation requires vessel certification and route authorisation. The Campania regional authority and the Port Authority of the Central Tyrrhenian Sea are natural first touchpoints.
seasonality: Peak season (Jun–Sep) drives the densest Bay of Naples traffic and the busiest hydrofoil schedules; the shoulder months (May, Oct) offer calmer crossings. A stabilised foiling craft holds its schedule through the summer swell that disrupts smaller craft.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to the Italian coast.
